A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JEPA-WM study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the revised organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original planning experiments, model ablations, quantitative comparisons, and qualitative rollout analyses on simulated environments and real robotic data.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results and adds data-scaling experiments, extended architecture/context comparisons, and final-checkpoint results across seeds.

M1.justification: V3 adds an AdaLN-zero variant with a zero-initialized conditioning MLP to the studied predictor configurations (Section 4). The selected AdaLN recipe, predictive losses, frozen encoders, and planning algorithms remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Metaworld training tasks, PointMaze, Wall, Push-T, DROID, Robocasa scenarios, and 16 collected Franka evaluation videos. V3's reduced-data experiments change training sample quantities within this coverage.

E2.justification: The conditioning comparison gains AdaLN-zero alongside AdaLN and the existing feature/sequence-conditioning variants (v1 Figure 6, v3 Figure 5a). DINO-WM, V-JEPA-2-AC, and the four planner comparators remain. The V-JEPA-2-AC bug fix and retraining were already documented in v1.

E3.justification: V3 introduces training-data fractions of 2%, 10%, 50%, and 100% with fixed iteration budgets, and extends context settings from W=7 to W=14, with Wall limited to W=9. Appendix E explicitly fixes iterations across context lengths, revising v1's explanation that longer contexts yield fewer gradient steps. This establishes a reported protocol revision without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds a systematic sample-efficiency study comparing the selected recipe with baselines across data quantities. Figure 5 extends long-context sensitivity and tests AdaLN-zero. These substantially broaden the design-choice analysis; equalized-action-ratio experiments, augmentation tests, and qualitative failure cases already existed in v1.

E5.justification: V3 Table 12 newly reports final-checkpoint variability across three training seeds, explicitly separating reproducibility across seeds from training stability. V1 reported across-epoch standard deviations after averaging seeds. Those temporal summaries remain, and the stated training-seed count stays at three.

E6.justification: V3 adds data-scaling curves, extended conditioning/context results, and final-checkpoint scores in Table 12. The headline table and full planner-comparison scores remain unchanged (v1 Tables 1/S5.1; v3 Tables 2/11). For example, the retained DROID aggregate for Ours is 48.2, while the newly reported final-checkpoint value is 46.5 under the different aggregation.

T1.justification: New Appendix D introduces three propositions and proofs concerning Lipschitz error bounds, affine tightness and nonlinear lower bounds, and sliding-window error propagation through a companion matrix. V1 has no corresponding theoretical analysis. Proposition 2(b)'s proof contains a single-point vector mean-value equality not justified by its stated assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the central claims: systematically studying JEPA-WM design choices and combining them into recipes outperforming DINO-WM and V-JEPA-2-AC. The principal conclusions about encoders, proprioception, context, model scaling, and planners remain.

C2.justification: V3 replaces the rollout-specialization explanation with a conjectured accuracy-versus-robustness tradeoff involving prediction error and effective Lipschitz constants. It expands encoder and scaling mechanisms, revises the context/data-loss explanation, and adds substantive limitations concerning deterministic MSE prediction of multimodal futures and cumulative-reward optimization.

D1.justification: V3 documents trajectory-level splitting, slice construction, DROID sampling/retry behavior, retained-data fractions, and explicit iteration counts. It also distinguishes training-rollout context Wt from W and Wp. Existing hardware, optimizer settings, training-time tables, and code/data/checkpoint access information are retained.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 and Appendix B substantially expand positioning against explicit versus implicit world models, reward/reconstruction-based methods, and encoder-adaptation approaches. Added discussions include TD-JEPA, EB-JEPA, PlaNet/Dreamer variants, and recent representation-learning work; some older citations, including LAPA and IQL, are removed.

P1.justification: The six-section main narrative and most technical appendix prose remain. V3 condenses introductory and related-work passages, rewrites selected result explanations, moves statistical details to Appendix G.2, introduces a notation guide, and revises author information and back matter.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a different publication layout with revised typography, margins, author arrangement, and figure sizing. It adds recipe, notation, and final-checkpoint tables plus the data-scaling figure, and regroups the architecture/context/model-size panels in Figures 5–6. Existing appendix visualizations are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The data-scaling study, separate across-seed final-checkpoint reporting, and clearer data-handling and applicability descriptions improve empirical assessability beyond v1. The headline results remain unchanged. These gains are tempered by the unjustified vector mean-value step in new Proposition 2(b) and a new recipe-table inconsistency: Table 1 recommends proprioception for real manipulation, whereas Section 5.3 omits it for DROID/Robocasa.
